title: 6EQUJ5
subtitle: The Wow! Signal · Ohio, 1977
voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.
grade: Desaturated documentary still, a 1970s university radio telescope observatory interior and the giant radio dish itself in a flat Ohio farm field at night, dim fluorescent control rooms with paper strip charts and 1970s mainframes, cinder-block walls, melancholy and uncanny, period 1977 detail, cinematic wide composition, fine film grain, no text, no signage, no people, no faces.

beats.vo: In August nineteen seventy-seven, a radio telescope in Ohio picked up a signal, from the direction of Sagittarius.
beats.img: A large 1970s radio telescope dish silhouetted against a heavy dusk sky over a flat Ohio farm field, distant treeline, eerie and quiet, no people.

beats.vo: It lasted seventy-two seconds. Then it stopped.
beats.img: A vintage 1970s radio observatory control room interior with paper strip charts on a table under dim fluorescent light, cinder-block walls, a single chair pushed back, no people.

beats.vo: Thirty times louder than the background noise. On the frequency of hydrogen, the most common element in the universe.
beats.cap:
30× the background
at the hydrogen line
beats.img: A close-up of a vintage 1970s paper printout strip with rows of printed letters and numbers including the sequence 6EQUJ5, dim desk-lamp light, documentary still, no readable annotations, no people.

beats.vo: The astronomer who found it on the printout circled the letters and wrote, in the margin, one word: wow.
Despite dozens of follow-up observations over fifty years, it has never repeated.
beats.img: A vast radio telescope dish array under a wide empty night sky with distant stars, low horizon, cold dim light, melancholy and unresolved, no people.
